messages:
maya: Quick RFC follow-up re: quant profiles lifecycle. We need a concrete split of responsibilities: who validates profiles (quality tests), who owns rollout/canary, and who triggers/falls back on degradations?

zach: I can start — runtime should own enforcement (selection, routing, fallback) and telemetry hooks. ML should own the profile artifacts + validation data.

liam: Agree. Also need a clear API contract between ML and runtime for 'profile readiness' and 'rollback signal'. Something like: `POST /api/v1/quant_profiles` + `GET /api/v1/quant_profiles/:id/status`. Payload includes quality thresholds.

sara: Important: include the eval set reference and a small shadow-sampling spec in the profile metadata. Otherwise ops can't reproduce regressions.

maya: +1. Proposal: ML publishes profile with `quality_floor`, `deg_score`, `anchor_prompts` (small list), and `shadow_sample_config`. Runtime reads profile, runs smoke checks, then canary.

kevin: For Dedicated customers we need an override/opt-out flow. Customer success must be able to pin a model+profile pair. Who gets the API to do that?

zach: Runtime owns pinning enforcement, but ML needs to produce an 'approved_for_pin' flag after internal QA. Pinning API should be auth-gated.

liam: Rollback triggers: automated rollback when rolling canary sees deg_score increase > 3 points OR human-visible error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m. We should parameterize those thresholds per-customer.

sara: We also want a 'soft-rollback' where we gradually lower traffic to the new profile and increase fallback. That reduces flapping.

maya: Ops playbook outline: 1) ML publishes -> runtime smoke tests 2) shadow sampling for 12h 3) canary @ 1% -> 10% -> 50% with telemetry checks at each step 4) full rollout or rollback.

on-technical detail: add an "ambassador" role on the ML side to own post-publish incidents and triage with runtime. This avoids ping pong.

kevin: Who implements the ambassador? Does it live in ML, or a shared SRE/solutions engineer? Customers will expect SLA response.

maya: Prefer ML product engineer as ambassador, but SRE oncall must be looped for infra-level issues. Ambassador owns quality threads.

oncall: Reminder: integrate alerts into #eng-oncall and include `deg_score` and `shadow_discrepancy_rate` in the alert payload. Avoid noisy alerts — use rolling windows + hysteresis.

infra-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary-rollout-service v2 will add `profile_id` in routing headers. Deploy ETA: 2026-03-25 18:00 UTC.

qa-bot: Pre-rollout checklist: unit tests for profile parsing, integration test w/ shadow sampling, smoke eval run w/ anchor_prompts, and a canary replay for 1000 samples. Marked as required.

zach: Interface note: runtime must expose metrics `quant.profile.applied`, `quant.profile.fallback_count`, `quant.profile.deg_score` with tags: profile_id, model, customer_id. ML needs to publish expected baselines for those metrics.

liam: One more: ensure profile blobs are immutable and content-addressed (hash). That way runtime can verify integrity and we can map rollbacks to exact artifacts.

sara: For telemetry privacy, strip PII in anchor_prompts and use hashed prompt ids. Document in profile schema.

maya: Next steps: zach & liam draft minimal API and metric spec by EOD Wednesday. kevin to draft pinning UX + auth flow. sara to provide sample anchor prompt redact rules. We'll reconvene Thurs 10am.

kevin: :+1:

sara: :eyes: will prep examples.

maya: Thanks all — good progress.
